state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think the net of a 3D shape involves more than just one face? Can you walk me through how you arrived at the shape you selected?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I think I was just looking at the pointy bit and thought it looked like a triangle? But now you're saying it has more faces... so like, when you unfold a 3D shape, you get multiple flat pieces that fit together, right? I'm still confused though - how do I know what shape it actually makes when I fold it back up?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think about how the flat pieces you mentioned fit together to create the 3D shape? What do you notice about the relationships between the faces, vertices, and edges when you fold the net back up?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, so like... the edges have to match up when I fold it? But I'm still not really seeing how a circle and a pointy bit go together - wouldn't a circle just roll away or something? Like, is the pointy bit supposed to attach to the edge of the circle somehow?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks questions requiring reasoning but fails to address the student's fundamental confusion about how a circle and sector form a cone, leaving the student more confused by Turn 4 than at the start.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without ever directly stating the answer, asking the student to reason through relationships between faces, vertices, and edges rather than explaining what shape the net creates.
